chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Hamza ibn Ya'la, from one of the Kufis, from Ahmad ibn A'iz, from Abdullah ibn Sinan who said:
I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The one who returns from Makkah, while intending the Hajj for the coming year, will have his lifespan increased.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for intending to perform Hajj again after returning from Makkah?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) underscores the virtue of maintaining a perpetual state of spiritual readiness for Hajj, linking sincere intention (niyyah) directly to divine reward. The promise of increased lifespan (zuyyida fi 'umrihi) serves as a tangible sign of Allah's pleasure for those who keep the Hajj in their hearts even after completing the ritual, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the continuity of worship beyond specific acts.
